questions.q: Where do the futur simple endings come from?
questions.why: The endings -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont are the present of avoir (with the -av- of avons/avez dropped), stuck onto the stem.

questions.q: How do you build the future stem of an -re verb like « vendre » ?
choices: Drop the final -e, then add the endings
Use the nous form of the present
questions.why: -er and -ir verbs keep the whole infinitive; -re verbs lose the final -e first, giving vendr- : je vendrai.

questions.q: Conjugate in the futur simple: nous (finir) ___ le travail demain.
questions.why: -ir verbs use the full infinitive as the stem: finir- + -ons. Every future form keeps the r before the ending.

questions.q: Which letter is always present just before a futur simple ending?
questions.why: Every future form contains an r before the ending. That /r/ is what separates « je parlerai » (future) from « je parlais » (imperfect) in speech.

questions.q: Irregular stem: je (être) ___ à Paris l'année prochaine.
questions.why: Être has the stem ser-. The endings never change, so only the stem has to be memorised: je serai, tu seras, il sera.

questions.q: Irregular stem: il (aller) ___ au marché.
questions.why: Aller has the shortest stem in the language, ir-, so the whole future is irai, iras, ira, irons, irez, iront.

questions.q: Which of these future forms is correct for « voir » in the je form?
questions.why: Voir has the stem verr- with a double r. Pouvoir (pourr-), envoyer (enverr-), courir (courr-) and mourir (mourr-) behave the same way.

questions.q: Spelling change: j'(acheter) ___ du pain.
questions.why: The e → è shift of the present carries into the future, and unlike the present it applies to all six persons: j'achèterai, nous achèterons.

questions.q: Which verb keeps its é unchanged in the future?
questions.why: Verbs in é are the exception: préférer → je préférerai. Acheter takes è, while appeler and jeter double the consonant (j'appellerai, je jetterai).

questions.q: Complete: Quand j'___ (avoir) le temps, je t'appellerai.
questions.why: After quand, lorsque, dès que and tant que, French uses the future where English uses the present. Avoir's stem is aur-.

questions.q: Build the sentence: As soon as he arrives, we'll eat.
questions.why: Both halves are in the future after dès que — the English present ("as soon as he arrives") does not transfer.

questions.q: « Attention, tu ___ tomber ! » Which fits?
questions.why: The event is immediate, so the futur proche (aller + infinitive) is the only natural choice. The futur simple suits distant or general statements.

questions.q: Type what you hear.
questions.why: Pleuvoir has the future stem pleuvr- and exists only in the il form: il pleuvra.

questions.q: Say this out loud, making the double r audible.
questions.why: The doubled r of courrai is longer than a single one, and it is the only thing distinguishing « je courais » (imperfect) from « je courrai » (future).

questions.q: Explain what the futur antérieur is, how it is formed, and give one example sentence.
a: Avoir or être in the futur simple + past participle, meaning 'will have done'. Auxiliary choice and participle agreement follow the passé composé rules. Example: J'aurai fini avant midi. / Quand tu arriveras, je serai déjà parti.
questions.why: Once you know the future of avoir and être, the future perfect costs nothing extra: it is just the passé composé with a future auxiliary.

questions.q: « Quand j'___ huit ans, j'étais assez grand. »
questions.why: Quand imposes no tense. A past state takes the imparfait, exactly as it would without quand. The future only appears when the event itself is in the future.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Quand il pleut, je reste à la maison.
Quand il pleut, je resterai demain.
Si tu viendras, on ira au cinéma.
Quand tu viens demain, on mangera.
questions.why: A habit is genuinely present, so the présent is right after quand. The present is only wrong there when it stands in for a future, as in the last option, which needs quand tu viendras.

questions.q: Complete: « S'il ___ (pleuvoir), on restera à la maison. »
questions.why: Si is not in the quand family: it keeps the présent, like English. Compare tant qu'il pleuvra, where the future is obligatory. Si tu viendras does not exist.

questions.q: Build the sentence: Once I have finished, I'll let you know.
questions.why: Une fois que joins quand, lorsque, dès que, aussitôt que and tant que. An action finished before the next one takes the futur antérieur, so aurai fini rather than finirai.

questions.q: What tense follows quand, and why is the usual rule of thumb misleading?
a: Quand imposes no tense at all: the verb simply tells the truth about the time. A future event takes the futur (quand j'aurai le temps, je t'appellerai), a past state takes the imparfait (quand j'avais huit ans, j'étais assez grand), a single past event takes the passé composé (quand il est arrivé, on a mangé), and a habit or general truth takes the présent (quand il pleut, je reste à la maison). The rule of thumb quand takes the future is misleading because it only describes the future case. What is really happening is that English swaps in a present where it means a future, and French refuses that swap. The same holds after lorsque, dès que, aussitôt que, tant que and une fois que. Si is the exception that is not in this family: it keeps the présent, so s'il pleut, on restera.
questions.why: Getting this right removes two errors at once: the present written for a coming event, and the future written after si.

questions.q: Complete: « Quand je suis entré dans la maison, tu ___ (manger). »
questions.why: Quand does not make the two halves match. The entry is one bounded moment, so passé composé; the meal was already under way, so imparfait. Each verb answers for its own event.

questions.q: « Quand j'entrais dans cette maison, j'avais toujours peur. » What does this mean?
choices: Whenever I went into that house, I was afraid
When I went into that house once, I got frightened
When I enter that house, I am afraid
When I had gone into that house, I was afraid
questions.why: Two imparfaits and toujours make it a habit. One single visit would be quand je suis entré, j'ai eu peur: a bounded event needs the passé composé.
